final_candidates.decision_summary: A387V adds a methyl group in the HA2 stem region near the N-terminus of the long alpha-helix, improving hydrophobic core packing and trimer interface stability. This is a well-established protein engineering strategy for thermostabilization.

G390A reduces backbone conformational entropy at the start of the HA2 helix, stabilizing the alpha-helical structure. Glycine-to-alanine substitutions are a classic helix-stabilizing strategy in protein engineering.

S375T is a conservative substitution adding a methyl group in the loop region connecting the HA1 head to the HA2 stem, potentially improving local packing or hydrogen bonding without disrupting the conformational change required for membrane fusion.

stop_reason.detail: After correcting invalid candidates and identifying three valid mutations targeting HA2 stem thermostability through established mechanisms, further self-iteration without external tools is unlikely to improve the Top-3.
